title: OpenAI: first look

claims.text: AI is the largest share of Accel's listed portfolio, at 48% across 15 companies.
OpenAI develops AI models and an API platform for developers, which matches Accel's AI focus.
Its business model is subscriptions and API usage, serving consumers, businesses and developers.
OpenAI reported $5.7 billion revenue in Q1 2026 and $6.7 billion in Q2 2026, according to the Wall Street Journal.
OpenAI closed a $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion post-money valuation.
OpenAI reported an operating loss of $12.3 billion for Q2 2026.
Reports say OpenAI is in talks to raise at least $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, while another report cites $1.2 trillion, so the valuation picture is unclear.
CEO Sam Altman said the company would not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns.
Accel's cheque size is not stated, so it is unclear whether a fund of its size could take a meaningful position in a round this large.
The dataset lists no confirmed stage or founding date for OpenAI, so stage fit against Accel's seed to Series D range is only estimated.

questions: What share of current revenue comes from API usage versus consumer and business subscriptions, and how is that mix changing?
What is the path from the reported $12.3 billion operating loss to profitability, and over what timeline?
Is the $30 billion round at $1.4 trillion still open, and what terms, minimum cheque and allocation would a new investor get?
How do the company's safety commitments and non-IPO stance affect expected exit timing and returns for investors?
Which reported valuation is current, and how does the $852 billion post-money figure relate to the later reports?
